pages.text: Geolosys names each deposit after its $(bold)mineral$(), the real name of that ore in the ground. The mineral tells you the metal: there is no iron ore block, there is hematite.$(br2)Shallow to deep. The next three entries give each ore: what it drops, where, and what it is for.

$(bold)Shallow:$()$(br)Malachite (copper) Y -16 to 90$(br)Coal Y 34 to 78$(br)Cassiterite (tin) Y 44 to 68$(br)Bauxite (aluminum) Y 48 to 65$(br)Hematite (iron) Y 32 to 60$(br)Sphalerite (zinc) Y 37 to 46, mountains

$(bold)Middle:$()$(br)Lignite (soft coal) Y -4 to 32$(br)Galena (lead + silver) Y -16 to 32$(br)Gold Y -64 to 32, dry land$(br)Platinum Y -25 to 19$(br)Lapis Y -64 to 64$(br)Azurite (copper) Y -49 to 13$(br)Cinnabar (redstone) Y -60 to 15

$(bold)Deep:$()$(br)Beryl (emerald) Y -56 to 19$(br)Bituminous coal Y -32 to -16$(br)Limonite (nickel + iron) Y -48 to -32$(br)Teallite (tin) Y -52 to -40$(br)Kimberlite (diamond) Y -64 to 10$(br)Quartz Y -64 to -48$(br)Anthracite (hard coal) Y -64 to -52

$(bold)Mining:$() ore drops $(bold)clusters$(), never raw ore. $(bold)Fortune$() gives more clusters. $(bold)Silk Touch$() gives the ore block itself.$(br2)$(bold)Processing:$() a cluster smelts to one ingot. A millstone or crushing wheels crush it, and washing (an encased fan through water) turns crushed ore into nuggets with a bonus. Uranium is not in this world.
